text:
incident-bot: PAGER: High KV/prefix cache miss-rate detected for tenant AcmeCorp in dedicated-pool-acme-prod — latency spike > 95th percentile. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/acme/caches?ts=1774501234 :rotating_light:
jamie (oncall): oncall here, acknowledging. I'll triage now.
jamie (oncall): initial read — 95th latency up from ~300ms -> ~1800ms, token cost up, error rate small but timeouts increasing.
marta (eng-sre): i'm awake, taking handoff if you want to escalate. what pool is this exactly?
jamie (oncall): dedicated-pool-acme-prod. metrics show global KV hit_rate collapsed from 0.82 -> 0.03 over last 10m.
kai (infra): any recent deploys or config changes to that pool?
jamie (oncall): there was a quick config flip in the admin console at 17:25 UTC to test a caching fallback for a different tenant. unsure if flag propagation touched acme.
marta (eng-sre): looking at admin logs now.
incident-bot: action required — oncall(s) acknowledged by jamie, marta.
marta (eng-sre): admin log grep: `PUT /flags/tenants/acme` @ 1774501500 by deploy-bot. payload: `{"kv_cache_enabled": false}` — oh.
note: this was meant for sandbox-tenant only but the flag scope resolution failed; flag applied to tenant namespace acme in dedicated-pool-acme-prod.
kai (infra): that explains it. cache disabled -> live traffic falls back to model compute every request -> hit-rate meaningless but latency skyrockets.
jamie (oncall): confirmed with quick API check:
```
# check cache status
curl -s -X GET "https://admin.internal/api/v1/pools/dedicated-pool-acme-prod/cache/status" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}"
# response (truncated):
{"kv_cache_enabled": false, "hit_rate": 0.03, "entries": 124}
```
marta (eng-sre): root cause candidate: flag scope bug in the flag-propagation service + a second issue: recent client change increased prefix cardinality (session-id appended to prompt key) -> even when cache enabled the effective hit-rate would be poor. both together tanked effective caching.
asha (solutions): customer-facing note: Acme's app saw model-side request latency > 2s and some retries. they're contacting CSM. I'll draft an update once we have mitigation ETA.
support-swift: recommend P1? customer-impacting, dedicated customer, production.
jamie (oncall): agree P1 for now. paging execs.
marta (eng-sre): mitigation plan (ordered):
1) re-enable kv cache for tenant (quick fix).
2) patch flag-propagation to prevent global/tenant scoping mixups (postfix patch).
3) short-term: apply prefix normalization rule on edge to strip volatile session ids for acme.
4) warm cache and monitor hit-rate.
5) schedule postmortem + permanent guards.

marta (eng-sre): re-enabling now (will run via admin API):
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/api/v1/tenants/acme/flags/kv_cache_enabled" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}" \
  -d 'true'
```
(marta executed admin call)
marta (eng-sre): also restarting cache gatekeeper on dedicated pool to pick up flag: `kubectl -n dedicated-pool-acme-prod rollout restart deployment/cache-gatekeeper`
marta (eng-sre): ran kubectl, pods are restarting.
jamie (oncall): doing quick smoke: 1 request sample before/after. before: 1850ms. issuing test request now.
(90s later)
jamie (oncall): after re-enable + restart: sample latency -> 410ms. hit_rate reported: 0.58 on metrics stream.
incident-bot: metric alert cleared for hit_rate threshold at 1774503300.
asha (solutions): sent short update to Acme CSM and support channel: "We see increased latency due to cache toggle, fix in progress. Will follow up with root cause and timeline."
support-swift: customer reply: they saw improvement but want assurance this won't recur.
kai (infra): temporary fix applied but we need to address prefix-cardinality. patching edge transformer to remove volatile session ids from cache key for Acme by setting `cache_key_template` to normalized form.

# quick patch to normalize keys (edge config snippet)
```
cache_key_template: "{tenant}:{model}:{prompt_normalized}"  # strip session_id and ephemeral fields
```
```
# small script to warm cache (run once)
python tools/warm_cache.py --tenant acme --model rwd-13b --prompts warm_prompts/acme_common.txt --parallel 8
```

marta (eng-sre): warming job kicked off (PID 8342). monitoring hit_rate.
(20m later)
marta (eng-sre): hit_rate stabilized ~0.67, 95th latency back to ~360ms, error rate normal.
jamie (oncall): logging timeline for postmortem:
- 1774501500: flag flip (intended for sandbox) propagated incorrectly to acme
- 1774501234: initial alert
- 1774501500-1774503000: escalation and triage
- 1774503000: kv cache re-enabled & gatekeeper restart
- 1774504200: hit-rate recovery observed

tom (eng-runtime): follow-ups: add integration test for flag scoping, add alert for sudden tenant cache hit-rate delta (>50% drop in 5m), and add canary check before global flag changes.
asha (solutions): customer wants timeline for root cause and remediation steps. i'm preparing a more formal summary for CSM + legal (VPC/dedicated contract).
support-swift: closing note — are we comfortable with P1 -> P2 downgrade? customer is seeing improved latency but they want postmortem.
marta (eng-sre): i'd leave P1 until postmortem posted.
jamie (oncall): handing off to marta for next 8hr oncall window. next oncall: marta (1774505400).
marta (eng-sre): taking over. scheduling postmortem meeting for 1774580000 (next-day 14:00 UTC).
tom (eng-runtime): i'll own the follow-up PRs for flag scoping and key normalization.
incident-bot: incident annotated: impacted_tenants=["acme"], severity=P1, mitigation=cache_reenable+prefix_normalization, owner=marta.
jamie (oncall): thanks team. updating ops-docs with the temporary mitigation steps.
marta (eng-sre): filing postmortem draft and linking playbook: https://docs.internal/ops/postmortems/1774501234-acme-cache-incident 
customer-monitoring: monitoring window open for 24h; will alert if hit_rate drops > 30% of baseline.
jamie (oncall): resolved for now — keeping thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
